source: The models’ skin tones are generally lighter, with a few outliers on either end.
claim: Across 262 cover appearances, measured skin lightness has a mean of 0.66 and a median of 0.67, ranging from 0.21 to 0.88.

source: On the far left you can see Lupita at the darkest end of the spectrum. Actress Anne Hathaway is on the far right at the lightest.
claim: Lupita Nyongo's 2018 cover has the lowest measured lightness (0.213) and Anne Hathaway's 2010 cover the highest (0.882).

source: Below, you’ll find the five darkest and lightest Vogue cover models of the past 19 years.
claim: The five darkest cover appearances are Lupita Nyongo in 2018, 2015 and 2014, Michelle Obama in 2009 and Serena Williams in 2015; the five lightest are Anne Hathaway in 2010, Jessica Chastain in 2013, Claire Foy in 2018, Amy Adams in 2014 and Natalia Vodianova in 2004.

source: You may have noticed something curious about the five darkest models: three of the faces (a full 60%) are Lupita’s.
claim: Lupita Nyongo accounts for three of the five darkest cover appearances, a 60% share.
code: f.nsmallest(5, 'l').model.value_counts().to_frame('count').assign(share=lambda d: d['count'] / d['count'].sum(), total=lambda d: d['count'].sum())

source: Alternatively, on the light end of the spectrum, we see five distinct faces.
claim: The five lightest cover appearances belong to five different models, each with one appearance among them.
code: f.nlargest(5, 'l').groupby('model').size().to_frame('appearances').assign(total_models=lambda d: len(d), total_appearances=lambda d: d['appearances'].sum())

source: Sixty-two models (50% of our dataset) have been featured at least twice.
claim: 62 of the 123 distinct models, 50.4%, appear at least twice.

source: Perhaps the best example of this is Rihanna. Across her five Vogue covers, her skin tone lightness spanned 40% of the lightness range that we found among cover models.
claim: Rihanna's five covers span 0.27 in lightness, which is 40% of the 0.67 range across all cover models.
code: f.groupby('model').l.agg(['count', 'min', 'max']).assign(span=lambda d: d['max'] - d['min'], overall_range=lambda d: f.l.max() - f.l.min(), share=lambda d: (d['max'] - d['min']) / (f.l.max() - f.l.min())).loc[['Rihanna']]

source: Between 2000 and 2005, there isn’t a lot of variance in how light the cover models appear. / After 2005 there’s a bit more spread.
claim: Skin lightness has a standard deviation of 0.076 across the 81 cover appearances from 2000 through 2005, versus 0.115 across the 181 after 2005.

source: And part of it is just Lupita. Her four recent appearances are responsible for tugging the trend towards the left.
claim: Lupita Nyongo's four cover appearances average 0.33 in lightness, against 0.66 for the other 258 appearances.

source: Gisele Bündchen (9 covers) Nicole Kidman (7) Sarah Jessica Parker (6)
claim: Gisele Bundchen has the most Vogue covers of any model, with 9, followed by Nicole Kidman with 7; Sarah Jessica Parker and Charlize Theron each have 6.
